claims.text: In central Europe, that carries you east at about 1,076 kilometres an hour.

Second, Earth circles the Sun at 29.8 kilometres every second.
That is about 107,000 kilometres an hour, a hundred times faster.

107,000 Earth around the Sun
Third, the Sun carries all of us around the centre of the Milky Way, at about 720,000 kilometres an hour.
Even so, one lap takes about 230 million years.

Even sitting still in central Europe, Earth's spin carries you at about 1,076 km/h, Earth's orbit at about 107,000 km/h (29.8 km/s), and the Sun carries us around the Milky Way at about 720,000 km/h. Each speed is measured relative to a different centre.

review.notes: Spin 1,076 km/h at 50 N computed from 40,075 km / 23.9345 h x cos 50 (equator 1,674); orbit 29.8 km/s from the planetary fact sheet = ~107,000 km/h, ~100x the spin; Sun 720,000 km/h and 230 million years per lap from NASA Sun facts. The compare note says each speed is relative to a different centre, so no one adds them up.
